title: Reduce policy flip sensitivity and harden stale variant handoff
creator: Arielle Chen
description: Summary: During a capacity pressure event on 2026-02-10 we observed a period of cross-region reroutes and a ~45m window where a subset of requests were routed to an incompatible model variant (quantized-8x vs fp16) causing repeated fallback attempts, token churn, and elevated tail latency. Investigation showed the policy election subsystem was flipping route weights faster than the variant compatibility cache could propagate, and stale handoff entries caused routers to retry to a previously-evicted variant. This ticket tracks follow-ups to reduce policy flip sensitivity and harden variant handoff correctness.
timeline: 2026-02-10 03:12 UTC - first customer SLO alerts for elevated 99th latency in eu-west1
2026-02-10 03:18 UTC - automated routing policy started shifting weight from f16-default to quant-8x-burst due to capacity constraint signals
2026-02-10 03:21 UTC - routers observed variant incompatibility on handshake; requests retried to alternative region; reroute amplification begins
2026-02-10 03:30 UTC - mitigation: emergency throttle added to policy recalculation frequency (manual change), reduced flip window from 30s->5m
2026-02-10 04:00 UTC - traffic stabilizes but some clients continued to see degraded throughput until 03:57 UTC
2026-02-12 - initial RCA draft completed and shared with Incidents channel
2026-02-14 - this ticket created to track hardening and action items
root_cause: Two contributing faults: (1) policy election used a low hysteresis config which allowed frequent weight flips during transient capacity signals; (2) the variant compatibility mapping cache had an asynchronous invalidation window (TTL=45s) and race conditions in the handoff path could return stale entries, causing routers to attempt handoffs to incompatible variants leading to retries and cross-region fanout.
steps_taken: Applied emergency config: increased policy election hysteresis from 10s to 5m to reduce rapid flips (hotfix) - reverted to safer defaults after stabilization
Disabled auto-promote of quantized variants for regions with <80% capacity utilization as a temporary control
Added a one-off migration to clear variant-compatibility cache entries in affected regions
Post-incident note: updated SLO dashboard to include variant-mismatch rate and fallback amplification metric
action_items: ENG-100212: Implement policy flip damping - change: add bounded exponential backoff on weight changes with configurable max frequency (owner: Diego Morales, est: 3) - due 2026-03-07

ENG-100213: Make variant-compatibility cache strongly consistent for handoff lookups - change: use validation handshake (version + checksum) before routing decision (owner: Lina Fischer, est: 5) - due 2026-03-21
ENG-100214: Telemetry: emit 'variant_handoff_stale' and 'fallback_amplification' metrics and add dashboard/alert at 0.1% (owner: SRE team - Priya Kumar, est: 2) - due 2026-02-28
ENG-100215: Add integration test that simulates rapid policy flips under capacity signals and asserts no cross-region retriable fanout (owner: Test Infra - Omar Valdez, est: 3) - due 2026-03-14
Update runbook: add step to pause policy recalculation and TTL-clear procedure (owner: Oncall RTE - Diego Morales, est: 1) - due 2026-02-28
postmortem_notes: Decisions: we will accept slightly slower policy reaction (increase hysteresis) to prevent oscillation cascades. Long-term we must decouple policy weight decisions from variant-compatibility propagation; the compatibility layer needs a strong validation API so routers can verify candidate variants before retrying. We also prioritize better telemetry and automated safeguards to prevent cascading retries.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on: (a) does the proposed compatibility handshake add unacceptable latency to tail requests? (b) are the new telemetry thresholds actionable? (c) do the integration tests adequately simulate region churn and TTL races?
customer_communication: Brief sent to affected customers on 2026-02-11 summarizing impact and mitigations; follow-up communication planned once hardening PRs are merged (owner: Samir Patel)
